"IMPOSTER — Completely Remove Typed Clue Mode

I want to remove the typed clue feature entirely and make the game use verbal clues exclusively.

I have attached two screenshots showing exactly what needs to be removed.

IMPORTANT: This is a focused feature-removal task. Do not change unrelated functionality, game mechanics, UI styling, or the Premium Editorial theme.

1. Remove the typed clue setting

In the \"Make it your game\" settings section:

Completely remove:

- \"Enable typed clue round?\"
- Its ON/OFF toggle.
- Its description: \"Players enter a clue on their turn before voting.\"
- Any related labels, controls, or explanatory text.

Do not replace it with another setting.

2. Remove the typed clue screen completely

Remove the screen shown in the first screenshot, containing:

- \"One clue. Keep it clever.\"
- \"NO SAYING THE WORD\"
- The individual player's typed clue turn.
- The \"Type a one-word clue...\" input field.
- The \"Give clue\" button.
- Any other UI elements exclusively used by typed clue mode.

This screen should no longer appear anywhere in the game.

3. Make verbal clues the permanent game mode

The existing verbal clue flow should become the default and only game flow.

The sequence should be:

1. Everyone privately reveals their role.
2. The Game Start screen appears and displays the randomly selected starting player.
3. The starting player taps \"START VERBAL DISCUSSION\".
4. The Discussion screen appears.
5. Players give clues aloud and discuss the secret word.
6. The existing \"CONTINUE TO VOTING\" button takes players to voting.
7. Existing voting and subsequent round mechanics continue normally.

There should be no typed clue phase between these steps.

4. Clean up related implementation

Inspect the code for typed-clue-only logic and remove obsolete functionality where safe.

This includes:

- Typed clue input state.
- Typed clue validation.
- Clue submission handlers.
- Typed clue-specific transitions.
- Typed clue-only conditional rendering.
- Any obsolete settings or stored state exclusively required by typed clue mode.

Do not remove shared game logic that is still needed by verbal clues, voting, or other features.

If older saved party settings contain a typed-clue preference, handle them safely so they do not cause errors.

5. Preserve existing verbal clue functionality

Keep:

- Random starting-player selection for every new round.
- Avoidance of the previous round's starting player whenever another eligible player exists.
- Existing party-level starting-player rotation between matches.
- Active-player eligibility.
- Discussion timer setting.
- Existing Game Start screen.
- Existing Discussion screen.
- Existing starting-player display and buttons.
- Existing voting, elimination, win conditions, and final guessing.

Do not accidentally reset or break starting-player rotation.

6. Preserve the existing design

Keep the Premium Editorial theme exactly as it is.

Do not redesign the settings page or game screens.

Maintain the existing colours, typography, cards, buttons, gradients, paper texture, spacing, and visual styling.

7. Testing

Verify:

- The typed clue setting no longer appears.
- The typed clue screen can no longer be reached.
- No typed clue input or submission button appears.
- The game always follows the verbal clue flow.
- Starting-player selection still works correctly for every round.
- Discussion can proceed to voting.
- Voting and all subsequent game mechanics still work.
- Existing parties and saved data remain intact.
- No obsolete typed-clue references cause runtime errors.

FINAL INSTRUCTION:

Remove typed clue mode completely, not merely hide its toggle. Make verbal clues the permanent game mode. Keep every other working feature unchanged. Do not redesign or refactor unrelated parts of the application.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

- Remove typed clue mode from IMPOSTER so verbal clues are the only clue flow while preserving gameplay and the Premium Editorial design.

## Requirements
- Remove typed-clue settings, screens, inputs, validation, handlers, transitions, and typed-only state or logic.
- Preserve role reveal → Game Start → verbal Discussion → voting, plus starting-player selection and rotation, timers, voting, elimination, win conditions, and final guessing.
- Keep saved parties safe, including older settings containing `typedClues`.
- Avoid unrelated functionality, styling, or theme changes; verify gameplay.

## Decisions
- No implementation decisions or changes have been made.

## Work State
### Completed
- Located typed-clue references in `app.js`, including settings, `clueIndex`, `clues` phase/render routing, and clue-feed rendering.

### Active
- Inspect phase transitions, round setup, and starting-player flow before removing typed-clue functionality.
- Determine safe handling for legacy saved settings containing `typedClues`.
- Verify preserved gameplay after implementation.

### Blocked
- None.

## Next Move
1. Inspect `app.js` settings handlers, typed clue rendering and transitions, and starting-player flow.
2. Remove typed-clue functionality and make verbal discussion the only clue flow; safely handle legacy saved settings.
3. Test verbal discussion, starting-player selection/rotation, voting, and subsequent gameplay.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Settings, state, rendering, phase transitions, and gameplay logic.
- `styles.css`: Existing styles; avoid unrelated changes.

## Important Context
- `app.js` defaults include `typedClues:true` merged with saved settings; state includes `clueIndex`.
- Render routing includes a `clues` phase; `renderDiscussion()` uses `state.clues` to display a clue feed.
- Role progression conditionally enters `clues` or `startingPlayer` based on `state.settings.typedClues` (around line 216).
- Preserve `startingPlayer`, `previousStartingPlayer`, and `verbalStarted` behavior.

import re
path = Path('styles.css')

obsolete = ('.clue-card', '.clue-top', '.turn-number', '.current-turn', '.pill-info', '.clue-feed', '.clue-item', '.discussion-card', '#clueInput')
rule = re.compile(r'([^{}]+)\{([^{}]*)\}')
def clean(match):
    selectors = match.group(1).split(',')
    kept = [selector for selector in selectors if not any(token in selector for token in obsolete)]
    if len(kept) == len(selectors):
        return match.group(0)
    if not kept:
        return ''
    return ','.join(kept) + '{' + match.group(2) + '}'
cleaned = rule.sub(clean, css)
path.write_text(cleaned)

## Objective
- Remove typed-clue mode from IMPOSTER so clues are verbal only while preserving gameplay and the Premium Editorial design.

## Requirements
- Remove typed-clue settings, screens, inputs, validation, handlers, transitions, and typed-only state or logic.
- Preserve role reveal, starting-player selection, verbal discussion, voting, timers, elimination, win conditions, final guessing, and starting-player rotation.
- Keep older saved settings safe, avoid unrelated changes, and verify gameplay.

## Decisions
- Delete legacy `typedClues` from loaded settings so old preferences cannot affect gameplay.
- Keep `.clue-entry` styles used by the final-guess form.

## Work State
### Completed
- Removed typed-clue UI, handlers, screens, state, discussion phases, and match-history clue recording from `app.js`; gameplay proceeds to verbal discussion.
- Removed typed-clue-specific CSS while retaining `.clue-entry` styling.
- `node --check app.js` and `git diff --check` pass.

### Active
- Verify timed and untimed discussion, voting, elimination, starting-player rotation, and final guessing in a browser.
- Review the final diff for unintended changes.

### Blocked
- Browser verification has not been completed; no `playwright`, `puppeteer`, or `jsdom` Node package was found.

## Next Move
1. Run browser-based checks of the verbal gameplay flow, including timed and untimed discussion and final guessing.
2. Review `git diff` and confirm no unintended removals.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Settings, phases, transitions, voting, and gameplay logic.
- `styles.css`: Typed-clue styles removed; final-guess form styles retained.
- `index.html`: App entry point and main container for browser verification.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; only `app.js` and `styles.css` are modified.
- The only remaining `typedClues` reference is the legacy-setting cleanup.

content.text:
playwright-cli - run playwright mcp commands from terminal

Usage: playwright-cli <command> [args] [options]
Usage: playwright-cli -s=<session> <command> [args] [options]

Core:
  open [url]                  open the browser
  attach [name]               attach to a running playwright browser
  close                       close the browser
  detach                      detach from an attached browser
  goto <url>                  navigate to a url
  type <text>                 type text into editable element
  click <target> [button]     perform click on a web page
  dblclick <target> [button]  perform double click on a web page
  fill <target> <text>        fill text into editable element
  drag <startTarget> <endTarget> perform drag and drop between two elements
  drop <target>               drop files or data onto an element
  hover <target>              hover over element on page
  select <target> <val>       select an option in a dropdown
  upload <files...>           upload one or multiple files
  check <target>              check a checkbox or radio button
  uncheck <target>            uncheck a checkbox or radio button
  snapshot [target]           capture page snapshot to obtain element ref
  find [text]                 search the page snapshot for text or a regexp, returning matching nodes with surrounding context (like search snippets)
  eval <func> [target]        evaluate javascript expression on page or element
  dialog-accept [prompt]      accept a dialog
  dialog-dismiss              dismiss a dialog
  resize <w> <h>              resize the browser window
  delete-data                 delete session data

Navigation:
  go-back                     go back to the previous page
  go-forward                  go forward to the next page
  reload                      reload the current page

Keyboard:
  press <key>                 press a key on the keyboard, `a`, `arrowleft`
  keydown <key>               press a key down on the keyboard
  keyup <key>                 press a key up on the keyboard

Mouse:
  mousemove <x> <y>           move mouse to a given position
  mousedown [button]          press mouse down
  mouseup [button]            press mouse up
  mousewheel <dx> <dy>        scroll mouse wheel

Save as:
  screenshot [target]         screenshot of the current page or element
  pdf                         save page as pdf

Tabs:
  tab-list                    list all tabs
  tab-new [url]               create a new tab
  tab-close [index]           close a browser tab
  tab-select <index>          select a browser tab

Storage:
  state-load <filename>       loads browser storage (authentication) state from a file
  state-save [filename]       saves the current storage (authentication) state to a file
  cookie-list                 list all cookies (optionally filtered by domain/path)
  cookie-get <name>           get a specific cookie by name
  cookie-set <name> <value>   set a cookie with optional flags
  cookie-delete <name>        delete a specific cookie
  cookie-clear                clear all cookies
  localstorage-list           list all localstorage key-value pairs
  localstorage-get <key>      get a localstorage item by key
  localstorage-set <key> <value> set a localstorage item
  localstorage-delete <key>   delete a localstorage item
  localstorage-clear          clear all localstorage
  sessionstorage-list         list all sessionstorage key-value pairs
  sessionstorage-get <key>    get a sessionstorage item by key
  sessionstorage-set <key> <value> set a sessionstorage item
  sessionstorage-delete <key> delete a sessionstorage item
  sessionstorage-clear        clear all sessionstorage

Network:
  requests                    list all network requests since loading the page. each request is numbered for use with the `request` command.
  request <index>             show full details (headers, body, response) of a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-headers <index>     print only the request headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-body <index>        print only the request body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  response-headers <index>    print only the response headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  response-body <index>       print the response body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command. textual bodies are inlined; binary bodies are saved to a file and the path is printed.
  route <pattern>             mock network requests matching a url pattern
  route-list                  list all active network routes
  unroute [pattern]           remove routes matching a pattern (or all routes)
  network-state-set <state>   set the browser network state to online or offline

DevTools:
  console [min-level]         list console messages
  run-code [code]             run playwright code snippet
  recording-start             start recording user actions
  recording-stop              stop recording user actions and print them as playwright code
  tracing-start               start trace recording
  tracing-stop                stop trace recording
  video-start [filename]      start video recording
  video-stop                  stop video recording
  video-chapter <title>       add a chapter marker to the video recording
  video-show-actions          annotate subsequent cli/mcp actions on the page with a callout that names the action and highlights the target element
  video-hide-actions          stop annotating actions performed on the page
  show                        show playwright dashboard
  pause-at <location>         run the test up to a specific location and pause there
  resume                      resume the test execution
  step-over                   step over the next call in the test
  generate-locator <target>   generate a playwright locator for the given element
  highlight [target]          show (or with --hide, remove) a highlight overlay for an element; `--hide` without a target hides all page highlights.

Install:
  install                     initialize workspace
  install-browser [browser]   install browser

Browser sessions:
  list                        list browser sessions
  close-all                   close all browser sessions
  kill-all                    forcefully kill all browser sessions (for stale/zombie processes)

metadata.displayText:
IMPOSTER — Fix the Imposter Hint System for ALL Secret Words

I have noticed an issue with the existing Imposter hint feature.


Currently, Imposters can receive hints about the secret word when the "Give Imposters word hints?" setting is enabled.


However, many words in the game's word database do not have their own dedicated hints.


For example:


- Secret word: Lion → The Imposter receives a useful hint.
- Secret word: Strawberry → The Imposter may not receive a suitable hint.
- Other words may have no hint available at all.


I want to fix this properly so that EVERY secret word can generate an appropriate, contextual hint.


IMPORTANT: Inspect the existing implementation first. Preserve all working game functionality and make only the changes required for this improvement.


1. Every secret word must have a hint


The hint system must support every word in every existing category, including:


- Animals
- Food
- Countries
- Cities
- Movies
- Sports
- Technology
- Objects
- Professions
- Celebrities
- Nature
- Transportation
- Random Mix
- Any other existing or future word categories.


Do not rely on a small manually maintained list of words with dedicated hints.


Every word selected by the game must be capable of producing a meaningful hint.


2. Build a reliable contextual hint system


Use a combination of:


A. Dedicated hints for words where precise hints are available.


B. Word metadata, including category, subcategory, attributes and related concepts.


C. Category-aware fallback rules that generate useful hints for words without dedicated hints.


For example:


Secret word| Possible Imposter hint
Lion| A powerful wild animal
Elephant| A very large animal known for its memory
Strawberry| A sweet fruit often used in desserts
Pizza| A popular shared food
Football| A team sport played with a ball
Eiffel Tower| A famous landmark in Europe
Bicycle| A vehicle powered by pedalling
Telescope| An instrument used to observe distant objects
Volcano| A natural formation associated with eruptions
Doctor| A profession related to healthcare


These are examples of the hint quality and contextual relevance I want.


Do not simply use the category name as the hint.


3. Hints must be useful without revealing the answer


This is extremely important.


A hint should help the Imposter understand the general subject without directly identifying the secret word.


Rules:


- Never display the exact secret word.
- Avoid obvious synonyms that reveal the answer.
- Do not make the hint so specific that the answer becomes immediately obvious.
- Avoid hints that are so vague they are useless.
- Prefer descriptions of characteristics, uses, environments, associations or general concepts.


The Imposter should receive enough information to participate convincingly, but still need to figure out the secret word from the other players' clues.


4. Automatically handle words without dedicated hints


This is the main issue I want fixed.


If a word does not have a dedicated hint:


1. Read its category and available metadata.
2. Identify its general characteristics or subcategory.
3. Generate a suitable contextual hint using the existing offline hint rules.
4. Validate that the hint does not contain the exact secret word.
5. Display the resulting hint to the Imposter.


There must never be a blank hint simply because a word is missing from a manually maintained hint list.


Do not use the old generic fallback:
"Think of a word that can be described in many different ways."


Instead, make the fallback specific to the actual selected word.


If a word genuinely lacks enough metadata, use a safe, category-aware description rather than inventing an unrelated characteristic.


5. Make the system compatible with future words


When new words are added to the word database, they should automatically work with the hint system.


Do not require developers to manually write a separate hint for every new word.


Where dedicated hints or metadata are provided, use them. Otherwise, use the contextual fallback system.


Keep the implementation lightweight and offline.


Do not introduce external APIs, paid AI services, network dependencies or unnecessary packages.


6. Keep hints consistent throughout a match


- All Imposters in the same match must receive the same hint for the same secret word.
- The hint must remain unchanged when navigating between screens.
- Do not generate a different hint every time an Imposter opens their role reveal.
- Generate or resolve the hint once per match and store it with the match state.
- A new match with a different secret word should generate its own appropriate hint.


7. Preserve the existing hint setting


Keep the existing "Give Imposters word hints?" setting.


When ON:


- Imposters receive the contextual hint.


When OFF:


- Imposters receive no word hint.
- The existing no-hint behaviour remains unchanged.


Do not change the role-reveal design or other settings.


8. Testing requirements


Test words from every existing category, including words that currently have no dedicated hint.


Specifically verify:


- Words with dedicated hints still work.
- Words without dedicated hints receive contextual hints.
- Hints match the actual secret word.
- Hints do not reveal the exact answer.
- Hints are not excessively vague.
- All Imposters receive the same hint.
- Hints remain stable throughout the match.
- The OFF setting still disables hints completely.
- Newly added words can use the fallback system automatically.
- No blank hints or generic fallback messages appear.


FINAL INSTRUCTION


Do not simply add more entries to the existing hint list.


Fix the underlying hint-generation and fallback architecture so that EVERY secret word in the game can receive a meaningful, relevant and non-revealing contextual hint.


Preserve the existing Premium Editorial design, role assignment, word selection, verbal clue flow, voting, scoring, party system, history and statistics.


Make only this improvement. Do not redesign or refactor unrelated systems.

## Objective
- Improve IMPOSTER’s offline hint system so every secret word receives a relevant, non-revealing hint that stays consistent throughout a match.

## Requirements
- Preserve the existing “Give Imposters word hints?” setting and role-reveal design; OFF must show no hint.
- Use dedicated hints and available word metadata where possible, with contextual category-aware fallbacks for all existing and future words.
- Never return a blank or generic hint, reveal the exact secret word, or make the answer obvious.
- Resolve and store one hint per match so all Imposters see the same hint across screens.
- Preserve gameplay and avoid unrelated changes; verify coverage, relevance, stability, and the OFF behavior.

## Decisions
- The existing hint implementation must be inspected before changes.
- No implementation decisions for the hint improvement have been made yet.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Improve IMPOSTER’s offline hint system so every secret word receives a relevant, non-revealing hint that stays consistent throughout a match.

## Requirements
- Preserve the “Give Imposters word hints?” setting and role-reveal design; OFF must show no hint.
- Prefer dedicated hints and available word metadata, with contextual category-aware fallbacks for existing and future words.
- Never return a blank or generic hint, reveal the exact secret word, or make the answer obvious.
- Resolve and store one hint per match so all Imposters see the same hint across screens.
- Preserve gameplay and avoid unrelated changes; verify coverage, relevance, stability, non-revelation, and OFF behavior.

## Decisions
- Retain dedicated hints when safe; use deterministic, category-aware fallbacks otherwise.
- Filter hints that contain the exact secret-word token sequence.

## Work State
### Completed
- Removed typed-clue UI, logic, state, and styles; retained `.clue-entry` styles used by final guessing.
- Added category-specific fallback hint lists, normalized exact-word detection, deterministic hashing, and revised `generateHint(word, category)` in `app.js`.

### Active
- Inspect hint assignment, storage, and display to confirm one hint is resolved per match.
- Verify hint coverage, relevance, consistency, non-revelation, and setting-OFF behavior.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect where hints are assigned, stored, and displayed in `app.js`.
2. Validate dedicated and fallback hints across categories, checking exact-word avoidance and match consistency.
3. Test that OFF shows no hint and run relevant syntax/diff checks.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Word database, hint rules and fallback implementation, match state, settings, and gameplay.
- `styles.css`: Prior typed-clue style removal; final-guess form styles retained.
- `index.html`: App entry point used for prior browser verification.

## Important Context
- `app.js` and `styles.css` have uncommitted changes from typed-clue removal; `app.js` now also has uncommitted hint changes. Preserve existing work.
- Earlier typed-clue verification passed `node --check app.js` and `git diff --check`; browser verification reported no uncaught errors.
- Latest `app.js` edit adds `CATEGORY_HINT_FALLBACKS`, `hintContainsSecret`, `hintHash`, and replaces `generateHint`. No verification of that edit has been reported yet.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Improve IMPOSTER’s offline hint system so every secret word receives a relevant, non-revealing hint that stays consistent throughout a match.

## Requirements
- Preserve the “Give Imposters word hints?” setting and role-reveal design; OFF must show no hint.
- Prefer dedicated hints and available word metadata, with contextual, category-aware fallbacks for existing and future words.
- Never return a blank or generic hint, reveal the exact secret word, or make the answer obvious.
- Resolve and store one hint per match so all Imposters see the same hint across screens.
- Preserve gameplay and avoid unrelated changes; verify coverage, relevance, stability, non-revelation, and OFF behavior.

## Decisions
- Retain dedicated hints when safe; use deterministic, category-aware fallbacks otherwise.
- Filter hints that contain the exact secret-word token sequence.

## Work State
### Completed
- Removed typed-clue UI, logic, state, and styles; retained `.clue-entry` styles used by final guessing.
- Added category-specific fallback hint lists, normalized exact-word detection, deterministic hashing, and revised `generateHint(word, category)` in `app.js`.

### Active
- Inspect hint assignment, storage, and display to confirm one hint is resolved per match.
- Verify hint coverage, relevance, consistency, non-revelation, and setting-OFF behavior.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect where hints are assigned, stored, and displayed in `app.js`.
2. Validate dedicated and fallback hints across categories, checking exact-word avoidance and match consistency.
3. Test that OFF shows no hint and run relevant syntax/diff checks.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Word database, hint rules and fallback implementation, match state, settings, and gameplay.
- `styles.css`: Typed-clue style removal; final-guess form styles retained.
- `index.html`: App entry point used for prior browser verification.

## Important Context
- `app.js` and `styles.css` have uncommitted changes from typed-clue removal; `app.js` also has uncommitted hint changes. Preserve existing work.
- Earlier typed-clue verification passed `node --check app.js` and `git diff --check`; browser verification reported no uncaught errors.
- The latest `app.js` edit adds `CATEGORY_HINT_FALLBACKS`, `hintContainsSecret`, and `hintHash`, and replaces `generateHint`; that edit has not yet been verified.

## Objective
- Improve IMPOSTER’s offline hint system so every secret word receives a relevant, non-revealing hint that stays consistent throughout a match.

## Requirements
- Preserve the “Give Imposters word hints?” setting and role-reveal design; OFF must show no hint.
- Prefer dedicated hints and available word metadata, with contextual, category-aware fallbacks for existing and future words.
- Never return a blank or generic hint, reveal the exact secret word, or make the answer obvious.
- Resolve and store one hint per match so all Imposters see the same hint across screens.
- Preserve gameplay and avoid unrelated changes; verify coverage, relevance, stability, non-revelation, and OFF behavior.

## Decisions
- Retain dedicated hints when safe; use deterministic, category-aware fallbacks otherwise.
- Filter hints that contain the exact secret-word token sequence.

## Work State
### Completed
- Removed typed-clue UI, logic, state, and styles; retained `.clue-entry` styles used by final guessing.
- Added category-specific fallback hint lists, normalized exact-word detection, deterministic hashing, and revised `generateHint(word, category)` in `app.js`.
- `node --check app.js` and `git diff --check` passed in the prior verification; latest attempt at coverage testing did not run because the VM lacked `localStorage`.

### Active
- Inspect hint assignment, storage, and display to confirm one hint is resolved per match.
- Verify hint coverage, relevance, consistency, non-revelation, and setting-OFF behavior.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect where hints are assigned, stored, and displayed in `app.js`.
2. Rerun generated-hint coverage checks with browser globals such as `localStorage` stubbed or by extracting the relevant declarations safely.
3. Test that OFF shows no hint and run syntax/diff checks.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Word database, hint rules and fallback implementation, match state, settings, and gameplay.
- `styles.css`: Typed-clue style removal; final-guess form styles retained.
- `index.html`: App entry point used for prior browser verification.

## Important Context
- `app.js` and `styles.css` have uncommitted changes; preserve existing work.
- The latest `app.js` additions (`CATEGORY_HINT_FALLBACKS`, `hintContainsSecret`, `hintHash`, and revised `generateHint`) have not had coverage validation.
- Coverage-test attempt failed with `ReferenceError: localStorage is not defined`; it reported no hint results.

## Objective
- Improve IMPOSTER’s offline hints so every secret word gets a relevant, non-revealing hint that remains consistent throughout a match.

## Requirements
- Preserve the “Give Imposters word hints?” setting and role-reveal design; OFF must show no hint.
- Prefer dedicated hints and word metadata, with contextual, category-aware fallbacks.
- Avoid blank or generic hints and hints that reveal the secret word.
- Resolve one hint per match so all Imposters see the same hint across screens.
- Preserve gameplay and avoid unrelated changes; verify coverage, relevance, stability, non-revelation, and OFF behavior.

## Decisions
- Retain dedicated hints when safe; use deterministic, category-aware fallbacks otherwise.
- Filter hints containing the exact secret-word token sequence.

## Work State
### Completed
- Removed typed-clue UI, logic, state, and styles; retained `.clue-entry` styles used for final guessing.
- Added category-specific fallback hints, normalized exact-word detection, deterministic hashing, and revised `generateHint(word, category)`.
- Validated hint generation across all 804 words: no missing, exact-word-revealing, flagged generic, or unstable hints.
- Corrected the Unicode normalization regex in `hintContainsSecret`; added additional fallback candidates if the primary fallback list is fully filtered.
- `node --check app.js` and `git diff --check` passed before the latest two edits.

### Active
- Rerun syntax, diff, and hint coverage checks after the latest edits.
- Verify hint assignment/storage and display behavior, including setting-OFF behavior.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Rerun coverage checks and `node --check app.js` plus `git diff --check`.
2. Inspect match hint assignment and confirm one stored hint is shared across Imposters; verify OFF displays no hint.
3. Review the final diff for unrelated changes.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Hint rules/generation, match state, settings, and role display.
- `styles.css`: Typed-clue style removal; final-guess form styles retained.
- `index.html`: App entry point for browser verification.

## Important Context
- `app.js` and `styles.css` have uncommitted changes; preserve them.
- Coverage testing uses Node’s `vm` to evaluate the `WORDS` and hint declarations without initializing browser storage.
- The previous coverage run passed for 804 words, but it preceded the latest normalization-regex and fallback edits.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Improve IMPOSTER’s offline hints so every secret word gets a relevant, non-revealing hint that stays consistent throughout a match.

## Requirements
- Preserve the “Give Imposters word hints?” setting and role-reveal design; OFF must show no hint.
- Prefer dedicated hints and word metadata, with contextual, category-aware fallbacks.
- Avoid blank or generic hints and hints that reveal the secret word.
- Resolve one hint per match so all Imposters see the same hint across screens.
- Preserve gameplay and avoid unrelated changes; verify coverage, relevance, stability, non-revelation, and OFF behavior.

## Decisions
- Retain dedicated hints when safe; use deterministic, category-aware fallbacks otherwise.
- Filter hints containing the exact secret-word token sequence.

## Work State
### Completed
- Removed typed-clue UI, logic, state, and styles; retained `.clue-entry` styles used for final guessing.
- Added category-specific fallback hints, normalized exact-word detection, deterministic hashing, and revised `generateHint(word, category)`.
- Fixed the Unicode normalization regex in `hintContainsSecret` and added emergency fallback candidates if the primary list is filtered.
- `node --check app.js` and `git diff --check` passed.
- Coverage check reported 804 words with no missing, exact-word-revealing, flagged generic, or unstable hints.

### Active
- Verify match hint assignment/storage and confirm one stored hint is shared across Imposters.
- Verify OFF displays no hint and review the final diff for unrelated changes.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect role-display paths to verify they use the stored per-match hint and suppress it when hints are OFF.
2. Review the final diff for unrelated changes and report verification results.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Hint rules/generation, match state, settings, and role display.
- `styles.css`: Typed-clue style removal; final-guess form styles retained.
- `index.html`: App entry point for browser verification.

## Important Context
- `app.js` and `styles.css` have uncommitted changes.
- The latest coverage run reported 804 words, with no missing, unsafe, flagged generic, or unstable hints.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Improve IMPOSTER’s offline hints so each secret word gets a relevant, non-revealing hint that stays consistent throughout a match.

## Requirements
- Preserve the “Give Imposters word hints?” setting and role-reveal design; OFF must show no hint.
- Prefer dedicated hints and word metadata, with contextual, category-aware fallbacks.
- Avoid blank or generic hints and hints that reveal the secret word.
- Resolve one hint per match so all Imposters see the same hint across screens.
- Preserve gameplay and avoid unrelated changes; verify coverage, relevance, stability, non-revelation, and OFF behavior.

## Decisions
- Retain dedicated hints when safe; use deterministic, category-aware fallbacks otherwise.
- Filter hints containing the exact secret-word token sequence.
- Restore the existing typed-clue gameplay rather than remove it as unrelated to the hint objective.
- Keep final-word-guess styles and behavior.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added category-specific fallback hints, normalized exact-word detection, deterministic hashing, and revised `generateHint(word, category)`.
- Fixed the Unicode normalization regex and added emergency fallback candidates when primary hints are filtered.
- Coverage check reported 804 words with no missing, exact-word-revealing, flagged generic, or unstable hints.
- Confirmed `startGame()` assigns `state.hint` once based on the hints setting; `renderDeal()` reuses it for each Imposter and shows no hint when OFF.
- Partially restored typed-clue state and setup UI after spotting its unrelated removal.

### Active
- Restore all remaining typed-clue and discussion flow removed by the current changes; inspect `renderDeal()`, clue-round functions, round transitions, match-history handling, and related `styles.css` removals.
- Recheck the complete diff and run validation after restoration.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Restore the remaining typed-clue behavior and associated styles while retaining the hint improvements.
2. Review the complete diff for unintended gameplay changes.
3. Run `node --check app.js`, `git diff --check`, and verify OFF behavior and same stored hint for all Imposters.
4. Report results and note uncommitted changes.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Hint generation, match state, settings, role display, and typed-clue/discussion flow.
- `styles.css`: Typed-clue and discussion styling removed in the existing changes.
- `index.html`: App entry point for browser verification.

## Important Context
- `app.js` and `styles.css` have uncommitted changes.
- Typed-clue UI, logic, state, and styles were removed; only some typed-clue pieces have since been restored.
- Earlier coverage results: 804 words; 388 dedicated hints, 416 fallbacks; zero reported missing, unsafe, flagged generic, or unstable hints.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Improve IMPOSTER’s offline hints so each secret word gets a relevant, non-revealing hint that remains consistent throughout a match.

## Requirements
- Preserve the “Give Imposters word hints?” setting and role-reveal design; OFF must show no hint.
- Prefer dedicated hints and word metadata, with contextual, category-aware fallbacks.
- Avoid blank or generic hints and hints that reveal the secret word.
- Resolve one hint per match so all Imposters see the same hint across screens.
- Preserve gameplay and avoid unrelated changes; verify coverage, relevance, stability, non-revelation, and OFF behavior.

## Decisions
- Retain dedicated hints when safe; use deterministic, category-aware fallbacks otherwise.
- Filter hints containing the exact secret-word token sequence.
- Restore typed-clue gameplay and its styles because removing it was unrelated to the hint objective.
- Keep final-word-guess styles and behavior.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added category-specific fallback hints, normalized exact-word detection, deterministic hashing, and revised `generateHint(word, category)`.
- Fixed the Unicode normalization regex and added emergency fallback candidates when primary hints are filtered.
- Hint coverage check reported 804 words, with zero missing, exact-word-revealing, flagged generic, or unstable hints.
- Confirmed `startGame()` assigns `state.hint` once based on the hints setting; `renderDeal()` reuses it for each Imposter and shows no hint when OFF.
- Partially restored typed-clue state and setup UI in `app.js`.

### Active
- Restore remaining typed-clue and discussion flow, including `renderDeal()`, clue-round functions, round transitions, match-history handling, and related `styles.css` removals.
- Review the full diff for unintended gameplay changes and run final validation.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Restore all remaining typed-clue behavior and associated styles while retaining the hint improvements.
2. Review the complete diff for unintended gameplay changes.
3. Run `node --check app.js`, `git diff --check`, and verify OFF behavior and consistent stored hints for all Imposters.
4. Report results and note uncommitted changes.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Hint generation, match state, settings, role display, and typed-clue/discussion flow.
- `styles.css`: Typed-clue and discussion styling removed in the existing changes.
- `index.html`: App entry point for browser verification.

## Important Context
- `app.js` and `styles.css` have uncommitted changes.
- Typed-clue UI, logic, state, and styles were removed; only some typed-clue pieces have since been restored.
- Recent restoration added `clueIndex`, `clues`, the `clues` and `discussion` render branches, and a typed-clue setup toggle.

## Objective
- Improve IMPOSTER’s offline hints so each secret word gets a relevant, non-revealing hint that remains consistent throughout a match.

## Requirements
- Preserve the “Give Imposters word hints?” setting and role-reveal design; OFF must show no hint.
- Prefer dedicated hints and word metadata, with contextual, category-aware fallbacks.
- Avoid blank or generic hints and hints that reveal the secret word.
- Resolve one hint per match so all Imposters see the same hint across screens.
- Preserve gameplay and avoid unrelated changes; verify coverage, relevance, stability, non-revelation, and OFF behavior.

## Decisions
- Retain dedicated hints when safe; use deterministic, category-aware fallbacks otherwise.
- Filter hints containing the exact secret-word token sequence.
- Restore typed-clue gameplay and its styles because removing them was unrelated to the hint objective.
- Keep final-word-guess styles and behavior.

## Objective
- Improve IMPOSTER’s offline hints so each secret word gets a relevant, non-revealing hint that stays consistent throughout a match.

## Requirements
- Preserve the “Give Imposters word hints?” setting and role-reveal design; OFF must show no hint.
- Prefer dedicated hints and word metadata, with contextual, category-aware fallbacks.
- Avoid blank or generic hints and hints that reveal the secret word.
- Resolve one hint per match so all Imposters see the same hint across screens.
- Preserve gameplay and avoid unrelated changes; verify coverage, relevance, stability, non-revelation, and OFF behavior.

## Decisions

## Objective
- Improve IMPOSTER’s offline hints so each secret word gets a relevant, non-revealing hint that remains consistent throughout a match.
- Preserve existing gameplay, including typed clues and final-word guesses.

## Requirements
- Preserve the “Give Imposters word hints?” setting and role-reveal design; OFF must show no hint.
- Prefer dedicated hints and word metadata, with contextual, category-aware fallbacks.
- Avoid blank or generic hints and hints that reveal the secret word.
- Resolve one hint per match so all Imposters see the same hint across screens.
- Avoid unrelated gameplay changes; verify coverage, relevance, stability, non-revelation, and OFF behavior.

## Decisions
- Retain dedicated hints when safe; use deterministic, category-aware fallbacks otherwise.
- Filter hints containing the exact secret-word token sequence.
- Restore typed-clue gameplay and styles because removing them was unrelated to the hint objective.
- Keep final-word-guess styles and behavior.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added category-specific fallback hints, normalized exact-word detection, deterministic hashing, and revised `generateHint(word, category)`.
- Fixed the Unicode normalization regex and added emergency fallback candidates when primary hints are filtered.
- Hint coverage check reported 804 words, with zero missing, exact-word-revealing, flagged generic, or unstable hints.
- Confirmed `startGame()` assigns `state.hint` once based on the hints setting; `renderDeal()` reuses it for each Imposter and shows no hint when OFF.
- Partially restored typed-clue state and setup UI in `app.js`.

### Active
- Restore remaining typed-clue and discussion flow, including `renderDeal()`, clue-round functions, round transitions, match-history handling, and related `styles.css` removals.
- Review the full diff for unintended gameplay changes and run final validation.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Restore all remaining typed-clue behavior and associated styles while retaining the hint improvements.
2. Review the complete diff for unintended gameplay changes.
3. Run `node --check app.js`, `git diff --check`, and verify OFF behavior and consistent stored hints for all Imposters.
4. Report results and note uncommitted changes.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Hint generation, match state, settings, role display, and typed-clue/discussion flow.
- `styles.css`: Typed-clue and discussion styling removed in the existing changes.
- `index.html`: App entry point for browser verification.

## Important Context
- `app.js` and `styles.css` have uncommitted changes.
- Typed-clue UI, logic, state, and styles were removed; only some typed-clue pieces have since been restored.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Improve IMPOSTER’s offline hints so each secret word gets a relevant, non-revealing hint that remains consistent throughout a match.
- Preserve existing gameplay, including typed clues and final-word guesses.

## Requirements
- Preserve the “Give Imposters word hints?” setting and role-reveal design; OFF must show no hint.
- Prefer dedicated hints and word metadata, with contextual, category-aware fallbacks.
- Avoid blank or generic hints and hints that reveal the secret word.
- Resolve one hint per match so all Imposters see the same hint across screens.
- Avoid unrelated gameplay changes; verify coverage, relevance, stability, non-revelation, and OFF behavior.

## Decisions
- Retain dedicated hints when safe; use deterministic, category-aware fallbacks otherwise.
- Filter hints containing the exact secret-word token sequence.
- Restore typed-clue gameplay and styles because removing them was unrelated to the hint objective.
- Keep final-word-guess styles and behavior.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added category-specific fallback hints, normalized exact-word detection, deterministic hashing, and revised `generateHint(word, category)`.
- Fixed the Unicode normalization regex and added emergency fallback candidates when primary hints are filtered.
- Earlier hint coverage check reported 804 words, with zero missing, exact-word-revealing, flagged generic, or unstable hints.
- `startGame()` assigns `state.hint` once based on the hints setting; `renderDeal()` reuses it for each Imposter and displays no hint when OFF.

### Active
- Restore typed-clue behavior: the setup toggle is present, but its change handler is missing; clue state initialization, clue-round routing, clue submission, and discussion flow are removed or incomplete.
- Restore associated clue styles in `styles.css`.
- Review the full diff for unintended gameplay changes and run final validation.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Restore the typed-clue toggle handler, clue state initialization, clue-round and discussion functions, and round transitions without changing final-word-guess behavior.
2. Restore the removed typed-clue styles in `styles.css`.
3. Review the complete diff; run `node --check app.js` and `git diff --check`, then verify hint coverage, OFF behavior, and consistent stored hints for all Imposters.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Hint generation, settings, match state, role display, and currently incomplete typed-clue flow.
- `styles.css`: Typed-clue and discussion styling was removed.
- `index.html`: App entry point for browser verification.

## Important Context
- `app.js` and `styles.css` have uncommitted changes.
- The latest inspection confirms typed-clue UI markup and `typedClues` default state remain, but the toggle handler and clue-related logic are missing; round progression goes to verbal discussion.
- `git diff --check` was run earlier and produced no reported errors; validation has not been rerun after the latest inspection.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Improve IMPOSTER’s offline hints so each secret word gets a relevant, non-revealing hint that remains consistent throughout a match.
- Preserve existing gameplay, including typed clues and final-word guesses.

## Requirements
- Preserve the “Give Imposters word hints?” setting and role-reveal design; OFF must show no hint.
- Prefer dedicated hints and word metadata, with contextual, category-aware fallbacks.
- Avoid blank or generic hints and hints that reveal the secret word.
- Resolve one hint per match so all Imposters see the same hint across screens.
- Avoid unrelated gameplay changes; verify coverage, relevance, stability, non-revelation, and OFF behavior.

## Decisions
- Retain dedicated hints when safe; use deterministic, category-aware fallbacks otherwise.
- Filter hints containing the exact secret-word token sequence.
- Restore typed-clue gameplay and styles because removing them was unrelated to the hint objective.
- Keep final-word-guess styles and behavior.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added category-specific fallback hints, normalized exact-word detection, deterministic hashing, and revised `generateHint(word, category)`.
- Fixed the Unicode normalization regex and added emergency fallback candidates when primary hints are filtered.
- Earlier hint coverage check reported 804 words, with zero missing, exact-word-revealing, flagged generic, or unstable hints.
- `startGame()` assigns `state.hint` once based on the hints setting; `renderDeal()` reuses it for each Imposter and displays no hint when OFF.

### Active
- Restore typed-clue behavior: the setup toggle is present, but its change handler is missing; clue state initialization, clue-round routing, clue submission, and discussion flow are removed or incomplete.
- Restore associated clue styles in `styles.css`.
- Review the full diff for unintended gameplay changes and run final validation.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Restore the typed-clue toggle handler, clue state initialization, clue-round and discussion functions, and round transitions without changing final-word-guess behavior.
2. Restore the removed typed-clue styles in `styles.css`.
3. Review the complete diff; run `node --check app.js` and `git diff --check`, then verify hint coverage, OFF behavior, and consistent stored hints for all Imposters.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Hint generation, settings, match state, role display, and currently incomplete typed-clue flow.
- `styles.css`: Typed-clue and discussion styling was removed.
- `index.html`: App entry point for browser verification.

## Important Context
- `app.js` and `styles.css` have uncommitted changes.
- The latest inspection confirms typed-clue UI markup and `typedClues` default state remain, but the toggle handler and clue-related logic are missing; round progression goes to verbal discussion.
- `git diff --check` was run earlier and produced no reported errors; validation has not been rerun after the latest inspection.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Improve IMPOSTER’s offline hints so each secret word gets a relevant, non-revealing hint that stays consistent throughout a match.
- Preserve existing gameplay, including typed clues and final-word guesses.

## Requirements
- Preserve the “Give Imposters word hints?” setting and role-reveal design; OFF must show no hint.
- Prefer dedicated hints and word metadata, with contextual, category-aware fallbacks.
- Avoid blank or generic hints and hints that reveal the secret word.
- Resolve one hint per match so all Imposters see the same hint across screens.
- Avoid unrelated gameplay changes; verify coverage, relevance, stability, non-revelation, and OFF behavior.

## Decisions
- Retain dedicated hints when safe; use deterministic, category-aware fallbacks otherwise.
- Filter hints containing the exact secret-word token sequence.
- Restore typed-clue gameplay and styles because removing them was unrelated to the hint objective.
- Keep final-word-guess styles and behavior.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added category-specific fallback hints, normalized exact-word detection, deterministic hashing, and revised `generateHint(word, category)`.
- Fixed the Unicode normalization regex and added emergency fallback candidates when primary hints are filtered.
- Earlier hint coverage check reported 804 words, with zero missing, exact-word-revealing, flagged generic, or unstable hints.
- `startGame()` assigns `state.hint` once based on the hints setting; `renderDeal()` reuses it for each Imposter and displays no hint when OFF.

### Active
- Restore the typed-clue toggle handler, clue state initialization, clue-round and discussion functions, and round transitions without changing final-word-guess behavior.
- Restore the removed typed-clue styles in `styles.css`.
- Review the full diff for unintended gameplay changes and run final validation.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Restore typed-clue behavior and associated styles.
2. Review the complete diff; run `node --check app.js` and `git diff --check`.
3. Verify hint coverage, OFF behavior, and consistent stored hints for all Imposters.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Hint generation, settings, match state, role display, and currently incomplete typed-clue flow.
- `styles.css`: Typed-clue and discussion styling was removed.
- `index.html`: App entry point for browser verification.

## Important Context
- `app.js` and `styles.css` have uncommitted changes.
- The latest inspection confirms typed-clue UI markup and `typedClues` default state remain, but the toggle handler and clue-related logic are missing; round progression goes to verbal discussion.
- `git diff --check` was run earlier and produced no reported errors; validation has not been rerun after the latest inspection.

input.command: git status --short && git diff --stat && git diff -- app.js

## Objective
- Improve IMPOSTER’s offline hints so each secret word receives a relevant, non-revealing hint that stays consistent throughout a match, without changing unrelated gameplay.

## Requirements
- Preserve the “Give Imposters word hints?” setting and role-reveal design; OFF must show no hint.
- Prefer dedicated hints and word metadata, with contextual, category-aware fallbacks.
- Avoid blank or generic hints and hints that reveal the secret word.
- Resolve one hint per match so all Imposters see the same hint across screens.
- Avoid unrelated gameplay changes; verify coverage, relevance, stability, non-revelation, and OFF behavior.

## Decisions
- Retain dedicated hints when safe; use deterministic, category-aware fallbacks otherwise.
- Filter hints containing the exact secret-word token sequence.
- Restore typed-clue gameplay and styles because removing them was unrelated to the hint objective.
- Keep final-word-guess styles and behavior.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added category-specific fallback hints, normalized exact-word detection, deterministic hashing, and revised `generateHint(word, category)`.
- Fixed the Unicode normalization regex and added emergency fallback candidates when primary hints are filtered.
- An earlier hint coverage check reported 804 words, with zero missing, exact-word-revealing, flagged generic, or unstable hints.
- `startGame()` assigns `state.hint` once based on the hints setting; `renderDeal()` reuses it for each Imposter and displays no hint when OFF.

### Active
- Restore the typed-clue toggle handler, clue state initialization, clue-round and discussion functions, and round transitions without changing final-word-guess behavior.
- Restore the removed typed-clue styles in `styles.css`.
- Review the full diff for unintended gameplay changes and run final validation.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Restore typed-clue behavior and associated styles from `HEAD`.
2. Review the complete diff; run `node --check app.js` and `git diff --check`.
3. Verify hint coverage, OFF behavior, and consistent stored hints for all Imposters.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Hint generation, settings, match state, role display, and currently incomplete typed-clue flow.
- `styles.css`: Typed-clue and discussion styling was removed.
- `index.html`: App entry point for browser verification.

## Important Context
- `app.js` and `styles.css` have uncommitted changes.
- Typed-clue UI markup and `typedClues` default state remain, but the toggle handler and clue-related logic are missing; round progression goes to verbal discussion.
- Recent diff review identified the removed clue flow and styles; no restoration edits have been made yet.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Improve IMPOSTER’s offline hints so each secret word gets a relevant, non-revealing hint that remains consistent throughout a match, without changing unrelated gameplay.

## Requirements
- Preserve the “Give Imposters word hints?” setting and role-reveal design; OFF must show no hint.
- Prefer dedicated hints and word metadata, with contextual, category-aware fallbacks.
- Avoid blank or generic hints and hints that reveal the secret word.
- Resolve one hint per match so all Imposters see the same hint across screens.
- Avoid unrelated gameplay changes; verify coverage, relevance, stability, non-revelation, and OFF behavior.

## Decisions
- Retain dedicated hints when safe; use deterministic, category-aware fallbacks otherwise.
- Filter hints containing the exact secret-word token sequence.
- Restore typed-clue gameplay and styles because removing them was unrelated to the hint objective.
- Keep final-word-guess styles and behavior.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added category-specific fallback hints, normalized exact-word detection, deterministic hashing, and revised `generateHint(word, category)`.
- Fixed the Unicode normalization regex and added emergency fallback candidates when primary hints are filtered.
- An earlier hint coverage check reported 804 words, with zero missing, exact-word-revealing, flagged generic, or unstable hints.
- `startGame()` assigns `state.hint` once based on the hints setting; `renderDeal()` reuses it for each Imposter and displays no hint when OFF.
- Identified that typed-clue markup and default state remain, while its handler, clue flow, and styles were removed.

### Active
- Restore the typed-clue toggle handler, clue state initialization, clue-round and discussion functions, and round transitions from `HEAD`, without changing final-word-guess behavior.
- Restore typed-clue and discussion styles from `HEAD`.
- Review the full diff and run final validation, including hint coverage, OFF behavior, and consistent stored hints for all Imposters.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Restore typed-clue behavior and associated styles from `HEAD`.
2. Review the complete diff for unintended gameplay changes.
3. Run `node --check app.js` and `git diff --check`, then verify hint coverage, OFF behavior, and per-match hint consistency.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Hint generation, settings, match state, role display, and incomplete typed-clue flow.
- `styles.css`: Typed-clue and discussion styling was removed.
- `index.html`: App entry point for browser verification.

## Important Context
- `app.js` and `styles.css` have uncommitted changes.
- The latest diff showed 61 changed lines in `app.js` and 36 removed/changed lines in `styles.css`.
- Typed-clue markup and `typedClues` default state remain, but the toggle handler and clue-related logic are missing; round progression goes to verbal discussion.
- No restoration edits or final validation have been performed.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Improve IMPOSTER’s offline hints so each secret word gets a relevant, non-revealing hint that stays consistent throughout a match, without changing unrelated gameplay.

## Requirements
- Preserve the “Give Imposters word hints?” setting and role-reveal design; OFF must show no hint.
- Prefer dedicated hints and word metadata, with contextual, category-aware fallbacks.
- Avoid blank or generic hints and hints that reveal the secret word.
- Resolve one hint per match so all Imposters see the same hint across screens.
- Avoid unrelated gameplay changes; verify coverage, relevance, stability, non-revelation, and OFF behavior.

## Decisions
- Retain dedicated hints when safe; use deterministic, category-aware fallbacks otherwise.
- Filter hints containing the exact secret-word token sequence.
- Restore typed-clue gameplay and styles because removing them was unrelated to the hint objective.
- Keep final-word-guess styles and behavior.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added category-specific fallback hints, normalized exact-word detection, deterministic hashing, and revised `generateHint(word, category)`.
- Fixed the Unicode normalization regex and added emergency fallback candidates when primary hints are filtered.
- An earlier hint coverage check reported 804 words, with zero missing, exact-word-revealing, flagged generic, or unstable hints.
- `startGame()` assigns `state.hint` once based on the hints setting; `renderDeal()` reuses it for each Imposter and displays no hint when OFF.
- Restored the typed-clue toggle handler in `app.js`.

### Active
- Restore the remaining typed-clue flow and styles from `HEAD`.
- Review the full diff and run final validation, including hint coverage, OFF behavior, and per-match hint consistency.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Restore typed-clue transitions, clue-round and discussion functions, and clue-related styles from `HEAD`, preserving final-word-guess behavior.
2. Review the complete diff for unintended gameplay changes.
3. Run `node --check app.js` and `git diff --check`, then verify hint coverage, OFF behavior, and per-match hint consistency.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Hint generation, settings, match state, role display, and incomplete typed-clue flow.
- `styles.css`: Typed-clue and discussion styling was removed.
- `index.html`: App entry point for browser verification.

## Important Context
- `app.js` and `styles.css` have uncommitted changes.
- The clue toggle handler was restored, but the clue-round flow and typed-clue round transitions remain missing.
- Current gameplay proceeds through verbal discussion.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Improve IMPOSTER’s offline hints so each secret word gets a relevant, non-revealing hint that stays consistent throughout a match, without changing unrelated gameplay.

## Requirements
- Preserve the “Give Imposters word hints?” setting and role-reveal design; OFF must show no hint.
- Prefer dedicated hints and word metadata, with contextual, category-aware fallbacks.
- Avoid blank or generic hints and hints that reveal the secret word.
- Resolve one hint per match so all Imposters see the same hint across screens.
- Avoid unrelated gameplay changes; verify coverage, relevance, stability, non-revelation, and OFF behavior.

## Decisions
- Retain dedicated hints when safe; use deterministic, category-aware fallbacks otherwise.
- Filter hints containing the exact secret-word token sequence.
- Restore typed-clue gameplay and styles because removing them was unrelated to the hint objective.
- Keep final-word-guess styles and behavior.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added category-specific fallback hints, normalized exact-word detection, deterministic hashing, and revised `generateHint(word, category)`.
- Fixed the Unicode normalization regex and added emergency fallback candidates when primary hints are filtered.
- An earlier hint coverage check reported 804 words, with zero missing, exact-word-revealing, flagged generic, or unstable hints.
- `startGame()` assigns `state.hint` once based on the hints setting; `renderDeal()` reuses it for each Imposter and displays no hint when OFF.
- Restored the typed-clue toggle handler in `app.js`.

### Active
- Restore the remaining typed-clue flow and styles from `HEAD`.
- Review the full diff and run final validation, including hint coverage, OFF behavior, and per-match hint consistency.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Restore typed-clue transitions, clue-round and discussion functions, and clue-related styles from `HEAD`, preserving final-word-guess behavior.
2. Review the complete diff for unintended gameplay changes.
3. Run `node --check app.js` and `git diff --check`, then verify hint coverage, OFF behavior, and per-match hint consistency.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Hint generation, settings, match state, role display, and incomplete typed-clue flow.
- `styles.css`: Typed-clue and discussion styling was removed.
- `index.html`: App entry point for browser verification.

## Important Context
- `app.js` and `styles.css` have uncommitted changes.
- The clue toggle handler was restored, but the clue-round flow and typed-clue round transitions remain missing.
- Current gameplay proceeds through verbal discussion.
- Recent attempts to search with `grep` for clue-related symbols failed with `ripgrep execution failed`; a `git diff -- styles.css` showed typed-clue styles removed.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Improve IMPOSTER’s offline hints so each secret word gets a relevant, non-revealing hint that remains consistent throughout a match, without unrelated gameplay changes.

## Requirements
- Preserve the “Give Imposters word hints?” setting and role-reveal design; OFF must show no hint.
- Prefer dedicated hints and word metadata, with contextual, category-aware fallbacks.
- Avoid blank or generic hints and hints that reveal the secret word.
- Resolve one hint per match so all Imposters see the same hint across screens.
- Preserve typed-clue gameplay and final-word-guess styles and behavior.

## Decisions
- Retain dedicated hints when safe; use deterministic, category-aware fallbacks otherwise.
- Filter hints containing the exact secret-word token sequence.
- Restore typed-clue gameplay and styles because removing them was unrelated to the hint objective.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added category-specific fallback hints, normalized exact-word detection, deterministic hashing, and revised `generateHint(word, category)`.
- Fixed the Unicode normalization regex and added emergency fallback candidates when primary hints are filtered.
- An earlier hint coverage check reported 804 words, with zero missing, exact-word-revealing, flagged generic, or unstable hints.
- `startGame()` assigns `state.hint` once based on the hints setting; `renderDeal()` reuses it for each Imposter and displays no hint when OFF.
- Restored the typed-clue toggle handler in `app.js`.

### Active
- Restore the remaining typed-clue flow and styles from `HEAD`.
- Review the full diff and run final validation, including hint coverage, OFF behavior, and per-match hint consistency.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Restore typed-clue transitions, clue-round and discussion functions, and clue-related styles from `HEAD`, preserving final-word-guess behavior.
2. Review the complete diff for unintended gameplay changes.
3. Run `node --check app.js` and `git diff --check`, then verify hint coverage, OFF behavior, and per-match hint consistency.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Hint generation, settings, match state, role display, and incomplete typed-clue flow.
- `styles.css`: Typed-clue and discussion styling was removed.
- `index.html`: App entry point for browser verification.

## Important Context
- `app.js` and `styles.css` have uncommitted changes.
- The clue toggle handler was restored, but the clue-round flow and typed-clue round transitions remain missing.
- Current gameplay proceeds through verbal discussion.
- Recent attempts to search with `grep` for clue-related symbols failed with `ripgrep execution failed`; a `git diff -- styles.css` showed typed-clue styles removed.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Improve IMPOSTER’s offline hints so each secret word gets a relevant, non-revealing hint that remains consistent throughout a match, without unrelated gameplay changes.

## Requirements
- Preserve the “Give Imposters word hints?” setting and role-reveal design; OFF must show no hint.
- Prefer dedicated hints and word metadata, with contextual, category-aware fallbacks.
- Avoid blank or generic hints and hints that reveal the secret word.
- Resolve one hint per match so all Imposters see the same hint across screens.
- Preserve typed-clue gameplay and final-word-guess styles and behavior.

## Decisions
- Retain dedicated hints when safe; use deterministic, category-aware fallbacks otherwise.
- Filter hints containing the exact secret-word token sequence.
- Restore typed-clue gameplay and styles because removing them was unrelated to the hint objective.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added category-specific fallback hints, normalized exact-word detection, deterministic hashing, and revised `generateHint(word, category)`.
- Fixed the Unicode normalization regex and added emergency fallback candidates when primary hints are filtered.
- An earlier hint coverage check reported 804 words, with zero missing, exact-word-revealing, flagged generic, or unstable hints.
- `startGame()` assigns `state.hint` once based on the hints setting; `renderDeal()` reuses it for each Imposter and displays no hint when OFF.
- Restored the typed-clue toggle handler in `app.js`.

### Active
- Restore the remaining typed-clue flow and styles from `HEAD`.
- Review the full diff for unintended gameplay changes.
- Run final validation, including hint coverage, OFF behavior, and per-match hint consistency.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Restore typed-clue transitions, clue-round and discussion functions, and clue-related styles from `HEAD`, preserving final-word-guess behavior.
2. Review the complete diff for unintended gameplay changes.
3. Run `node --check app.js` and `git diff --check`, then verify hint coverage, OFF behavior, and per-match hint consistency.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Hint generation, settings, match state, role display, and incomplete typed-clue flow.
- `styles.css`: Typed-clue and discussion styling was removed.
- `index.html`: App entry point for browser verification.

## Important Context
- `app.js` and `styles.css` have uncommitted changes.
- The clue toggle handler was restored, but the clue-round flow and typed-clue round transitions remain missing.
- Current gameplay proceeds through verbal discussion.
- Recent attempts to search with `grep` for clue-related symbols failed with `ripgrep execution failed`; a `git diff -- styles.css` showed typed-clue styles removed.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Improve IMPOSTER’s offline hints so each secret word gets a relevant, non-revealing hint that remains consistent throughout a match, without unrelated gameplay changes.

## Requirements

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Improve IMPOSTER’s offline hints so each secret word gets a relevant, non-revealing hint that remains consistent throughout a match, without unrelated gameplay changes.

## Requirements
- Preserve the “Give Imposters word hints?” setting and role-reveal design; OFF must show no hint.
- Prefer dedicated hints and word metadata, with contextual, category-aware fallbacks.
- Avoid blank or generic hints and hints that reveal the secret word.
- Resolve one hint per match so all Imposters see the same hint across screens.
- Preserve typed-clue gameplay and final-word-guess styles and behavior.

## Decisions
- Retain dedicated hints when safe; use deterministic, category-aware fallbacks otherwise.
- Filter hints containing the exact secret-word token sequence.
- Restore typed-clue gameplay and styles because removing them was unrelated to the hint objective.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added category-specific fallback hints, normalized exact-word detection, deterministic hashing, and revised `generateHint(word, category)`.
- Fixed the Unicode normalization regex and added emergency fallback candidates when primary hints are filtered.
- An earlier hint coverage check reported 804 words, with zero missing, exact-word-revealing, flagged generic, or unstable hints.
- `startGame()` assigns `state.hint` once based on the hints setting; `renderDeal()` reuses it for each Imposter and displays no hint when OFF.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Improve IMPOSTER’s offline hints so each secret word gets a relevant, non-revealing hint that remains consistent throughout a match, without unrelated gameplay changes.

## Requirements
- Preserve the “Give Imposters word hints?” setting and role-reveal design; OFF must show no hint.
- Prefer dedicated hints and word metadata, with contextual, category-aware fallbacks.
- Avoid blank or generic hints and hints that reveal the secret word.
- Resolve one hint per match so all Imposters see the same hint across screens.
- Preserve typed-clue gameplay and final-word-guess styles and behavior.

## Decisions
- Retain dedicated hints when safe; use deterministic, category-aware fallbacks otherwise.
- Filter hints containing the exact secret-word token sequence.
- Restore typed-clue gameplay and styles because removing them was unrelated to the hint objective.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added category-specific fallback hints, normalized exact-word detection, deterministic hashing, and revised `generateHint(word, category)`.
- Fixed the Unicode normalization regex and added emergency fallback candidates when primary hints are filtered.
- An earlier hint coverage check reported 804 words, with zero missing, exact-word-revealing, flagged generic, or unstable hints.
- `startGame()` assigns `state.hint` once based on the hints setting; `renderDeal()` reuses it for each Imposter and displays no hint when OFF.
- Restored the typed-clue toggle handler in `app.js`.

### Active
- Restore the remaining typed-clue flow and styles from `HEAD`.
- Review the full diff for unintended gameplay changes.
- Run final validation, including hint coverage, OFF behavior, and per-match hint consistency.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Restore typed-clue transitions, clue-round and discussion functions, and clue-related styles from `HEAD`, preserving final-word-guess behavior.
2. Review the complete diff for unintended gameplay changes.
3. Run `node --check app.js` and `git diff --check`, then verify hint coverage, OFF behavior, and per-match hint consistency.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Hint generation, settings, match state, role display, and incomplete typed-clue flow.
- `styles.css`: Typed-clue and discussion styling was removed.
- `index.html`: App entry point for browser verification.

## Important Context
- `app.js` and `styles.css` have uncommitted changes; latest `git status --short` showed both modified.
- The clue toggle handler was restored, but the clue-round flow and typed-clue round transitions remain missing.
- Current gameplay proceeds through verbal discussion.
- Recent attempts to search with `grep` for clue-related symbols failed with `ripgrep execution failed`; a `git diff -- styles.css` showed typed-clue styles removed.

input.command: sed -n '235,265p' app.js && git show HEAD:app.js | sed -n '205,232p'

grep -nE 'clue-card|clue-entry|clue-feed|clue-item|discussion-card|timer|starting-player|verbal|start-discussion' styles.css; git diff --unified=0 -- styles.css | head -80; git diff --unified=3 -- app.js | tail -100

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Improve IMPOSTER’s offline hints so each secret word gets a relevant, non-revealing hint that remains consistent throughout a match, without unrelated gameplay changes.

## Requirements
- Preserve the “Give Imposters word hints?” setting and role-reveal design; OFF must show no hint.
- Prefer dedicated hints and word metadata, with contextual, category-aware fallbacks.
- Avoid blank or generic hints and hints that reveal the secret word.
- Resolve one hint per match so all Imposters see the same hint across screens.
- Preserve typed-clue gameplay and final-word-guess styles and behavior.

## Decisions
- Retain dedicated hints when safe; use deterministic, category-aware fallbacks otherwise.
- Filter hints containing the exact secret-word token sequence.
- Restore typed-clue gameplay and styles because removing them was unrelated to the hint objective.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added category-specific fallback hints, normalized exact-word detection, deterministic hashing, and revised `generateHint(word, category)`.
- Fixed the Unicode normalization regex and added emergency fallback candidates when primary hints are filtered.
- An earlier hint coverage check reported 804 words, with zero missing, exact-word-revealing, flagged generic, or unstable hints.
- `startGame()` assigns `state.hint` once based on the hints setting; `renderDeal()` reuses it for each Imposter and displays no hint when OFF.
- Restored the typed-clue toggle handler in `app.js`.

### Active
- Restore the remaining typed-clue flow and styles from `HEAD`.
- Review the full diff for unintended gameplay changes.
- Run final validation, including hint coverage, OFF behavior, and per-match hint consistency.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Restore typed-clue transitions, clue-round and discussion functions, and clue-related styles from `HEAD`, preserving final-word-guess behavior.
2. Review the complete diff for unintended gameplay changes.
3. Run `node --check app.js` and `git diff --check`, then verify hint coverage, OFF behavior, and per-match hint consistency.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Hint generation, settings, match state, role display, and incomplete typed-clue flow.
- `styles.css`: Typed-clue and discussion styling was removed.
- `index.html`: App entry point for browser verification.

## Important Context
- `app.js` and `styles.css` have uncommitted changes; latest `git status --short` showed both modified.
- The clue toggle handler was restored, but the clue-round flow and typed-clue round transitions remain missing.
- Current gameplay proceeds through verbal discussion.
- Recent attempts to search with `grep` for clue-related symbols failed with `ripgrep execution failed`; a `git diff -- styles.css` showed typed-clue styles removed.

input.command: git diff -- app.js | tail -n 160 && git diff -- styles.css | tail -n 80

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Improve IMPOSTER’s offline hints so each secret word gets a relevant, non-revealing hint that remains consistent throughout a match, without unrelated gameplay changes.

## Requirements
- Preserve the “Give Imposters word hints?” setting and role-reveal design; OFF must show no hint.
- Prefer dedicated hints and word metadata, with contextual, category-aware fallbacks.
- Avoid blank or generic hints and hints that reveal the secret word.
- Resolve one hint per match so all Imposters see the same hint across screens.
- Preserve typed-clue gameplay and final-word-guess styles and behavior.

## Decisions
- Retain dedicated hints when safe; use deterministic, category-aware fallbacks otherwise.
- Filter hints containing the exact secret-word token sequence.
- Restore typed-clue gameplay and styles because removing them was unrelated to the hint objective.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added category-specific fallback hints, normalized exact-word detection, deterministic hashing, and revised `generateHint(word, category)`.
- Fixed the Unicode normalization regex and added emergency fallback candidates when primary hints are filtered.
- An earlier hint coverage check reported 804 words, with zero missing, exact-word-revealing, flagged generic, or unstable hints.
- `startGame()` assigns `state.hint` once based on the hints setting; `renderDeal()` reuses it for each Imposter and displays no hint when OFF.
- Restored the typed-clue toggle handler in `app.js`.

### Active
- Restore the remaining typed-clue flow and styles from `HEAD`.
- Review the full diff for unintended gameplay changes.
- Run final validation, including hint coverage, OFF behavior, and per-match hint consistency.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Restore typed-clue transitions, clue-round and discussion functions, and clue-related styles from `HEAD`, preserving final-word-guess behavior.
2. Review the complete diff for unintended gameplay changes.
3. Run `node --check app.js` and `git diff --check`, then verify hint coverage, OFF behavior, and per-match hint consistency.

## Relevant Files
- `app.js`: Hint generation, settings, match state, role display, and incomplete typed-clue flow.
- `styles.css`: Typed-clue and discussion styling was removed.
- `index.html`: App entry point for browser verification.

## Important Context
- `app.js` and `styles.css` have uncommitted changes; latest `git status --short` showed both modified.
- The clue toggle handler was restored, but the clue-round flow and typed-clue round transitions remain missing.
- Current gameplay proceeds through verbal discussion.
